previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for acute respiratory distress due to fluid overload from acute-on-chronic diastolic heart failure. She presented with severe hypertension and pulmonary edema, requiring emergent hemodialysis with removal of approximately 3 liters of fluid. A central line was placed in the left femoral vein due to difficult IV access, later removed without complication. Her symptoms improved rapidly post-dialysis, and she was weaned off respiratory support. A urinary tract infection with Enterococcus was identified and treated with levofloxacin, while infectious workup for pneumonia was negative. She remained hemodynamically stable with normal cardiac enzymes and was discharged home on her baseline medications with adjustments to warfarin dosing and instructions to complete a short course of antibiotics and monitor INR closely.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with CHF exacerbation.  Assess for CHF.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

PORTABLE AP CHEST:  The cardiac silhouette is enlarged.  Widening of the
vascular pedicle and prominence of the pulmonary vascularity is likely
reflective of underlying edema.  Small to bilateral pleural effusions are also
evident.  The lungs are otherwise clear.  A faint opacity projecting over the
right lung apex may represent a summation of shadows. The outline of a stent
projects over the left mid arm.

IMPRESSION:  1. Mild-to-moderate congestive heart failure. 2. Right apical
faint opacity, likely summation artifact. Short interval follow-up CXR or
chest CT is recommended to exclude underlying lesion.

HISTORY:  Shortness of breath.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, there is persistent enlargement
of the cardiac silhouette with tortuosity of the aorta.  Evidence of elevated
pulmonary venous pressure along with substantial bilateral pleural effusions. 
The findings are consistent with the clinical diagnosis of congestive failure.

The questioned right apical opacity is difficult to appreciate on this study,
though it could merely be covered by overlapping bony shadows.  This area
should be closely evaluated when the patient's condition improves.

IMPRESSION:  Congestive failure.
